root_cause.text: In `xfrm6_rcv_encap()` the IPv6 route lookup (`ip6_route_input_lookup()`) returns a referenced `dst` even for error routes, but the `dst->error` path dropped the skb without calling `dst_release()`, causing a destination entry reference leak in `net/ipv6/xfrm6_protocol.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `dst_release(dst);` immediately before `goto drop;` inside `xfrm6_rcv_encap()` when `dst->error` is true, and the CVE description explicitly says the function “drops the skb without attaching the dst to the skb and without releasing the reference returned by the lookup,” leading to leaked dst entries on repeated packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the route lookup destination on error to fix a reference leak in xfrm6 encapsulation receive handling.
intent_record.what: The code adds braces around the `if (dst->error)` block and inserts a `dst_release(dst);` call before jumping to `drop` when the route lookup result contains an error.
intent_record.how: When route lookup fails, the acquired destination entry is now explicitly released before error handling continues, preventing the error path from leaking the `dst` reference and ensuring proper cleanup at runtime.

candidates.rationale: This is the error check that leads to the drop path after ip6_route_input_lookup() returns a referenced dst. In the buggy code, taking this branch discarded the skb without releasing the acquired dst reference.
This jump is the direct control-flow action that exits on dst->error. The root cause is that this error path omitted dst_release(), so the destination entry reference leaked.
This call obtains the referenced route destination. Since the returned dst is later dropped on error without release, this allocation-like acquisition is part of the leak source.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the error-path branch taken after ip6_route_input_lookup() returns a referenced dst. In the vulnerable code, this branch led to dropping the skb without first releasing the acquired destination reference.
This control transfer exits on the dst->error path, and in the buggy version it bypassed any dst_release() call, causing the referenced dst to leak.

This lookup acquires the route destination reference that must later be released. The vulnerability manifests because the returned referenced dst was dropped on the error path without a corresponding dst_release().
